summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute watery diarrhea and hypoxia. He had been evaluated earlier the same day for Foley catheter discomfort, but his urinalysis was unremarkable. Shortly after discharge, he developed multiple episodes of non-bloody diarrhea and worsening shortness of breath. In the ED, he was found to have oxygen saturation dropping to 90-92% on room air. A chest X-ray revealed a right lower lobe opacity, suspicious for pneumonia. He was started on IV levofloxacin and admitted. Diarrhea resolved spontaneously, and stool studies for C. diff, ova and parasites, and bacterial pathogens were negative. Blood cultures showed no growth. His oxygen levels improved, and he was weaned off supplemental oxygen. He completed a course of antibiotics and was discharged home with instructions to finish oral levofloxacin, obtain a follow-up chest X-ray, and attend scheduled urology and primary care appointments. His chronic conditions remained stable.
